spatial_claims.claim: E is the intersection of diagonals AC and BD of square ABCD; E lies on both AC and BD
ABCD is equilateral (DA = AB = BC = CD) and right-angled (all angles are right angles)
Triangles DAB and CBA are congruent by SAS; angle ABD = angle BAC; since E lies on BD and AC, angle EBA = angle EAB
Triangle EAB has equal base angles EAB and EBA, so EA = EB by I.6
Triangle EBC has equal base angles ECB and EBC, so EC = EB by I.6
Triangle ECD has equal base angles EDC and ECD, so ED = EC by I.6
EA = EB = EC = ED by transitivity
Circle centered at E with radius EA passes through all four vertices A, B, C, D

configuration_map: Point E is the intersection of diagonals AC and BD of square ABCD. E lies at the center of the square, interior to it, and equidistant from all four vertices. E is not on any side of the square, so triangles EAB, EBC, ECD, and EDA are all well-defined non-degenerate triangles. The diagonals divide the square into four congruent right isosceles triangles. No point changes position or takes on contradictory roles across steps.
pass_reason: The proof makes straightforward spatial claims about the intersection of diagonals of a square and uses SAS congruence (I.4) and isosceles triangle properties (I.6) in a standard, correct manner. No angle decomposition is performed, avoiding the primary error pattern. All spatial claims — E on both diagonals, the SAS congruences of adjacent triangles, the angle re-labelings, and the equal distance conclusions — are mutually consistent throughout.
